actions.label: Resolve party
actions.description: Find or create the friend record for an external identity.
actions.agent: Resolve an external identity (provider + externalId on a channel) into a friend record, creating one on first contact. Returns { friend, channel, created }.
actions.when: First contact on any channel: turn whoever is talking into their friend record, made new when unseen

errors.means: The provider or external id is empty or invalid, a record file could not be read or written, or two records claim the same identity; the message says which.
errors.fix: Pass a non-empty provider and externalId; if they are set, check the file the message names in the friends directory and resolve the party again.

provider.label: Provider
provider.description: identity provider, e.g. aad, local, teams-conversation, imessage-handle, email-address, a2a-agent

externalId.label: External id
externalId.description: the external identity within the provider

displayName.label: Display name
displayName.description: display name for the party (use 'Unknown' if not known)

channel.label: Channel
channel.description: the channel/sense the session belongs to, e.g. cli, teams, mcp

actions.label: Describe trust
actions.description: Explain how much a friend is trusted and why.
actions.agent: Explain the trust context for a friend: level, basis (direct/shared_group/unknown), what it permits and constrains.
actions.when: Deciding how openly to talk with someone: their trust level, its basis, and what that level permits

errors.means: No friend record has that uuid or name, or two share the name, so there is no trust to explain.
errors.fix: Call list_friends to find the record, then describe its trust by uuid or name.

errors.means: The record's file could not be read or parsed when looked up by uuid; the message says why.
errors.fix: Check the file the message names in the friends directory, then describe the trust again.

isGroupChat.label: Group chat
isGroupChat.description: set to 'true' when the conversation is a group chat

actions.label: Assess standing
actions.description: Judge a peer's standing from your own past outcomes with them.
actions.agent: Assess a peer's earned standing from your FIRST-PARTY outcomes with them: a tier (proven/reliable/mixed/untested/troubled), the basis count, and the tally. Advisory only: it changes no trust and is not shared. Returns a Standing, or { ok:false, status:'not_found' } when the friend is missing.
actions.when: Weighing a peer's track record as data: a tier and tally from this agent's own past outcomes with them

errors.means: No friend record has that uuid or name, or two share the name, so there is no track record to tally.
errors.fix: Call list_friends with kind agent to find the peer, then assess it by id.

errors.means: The peer's record file could not be read or parsed when looked up by uuid; the message says why.
errors.fix: Check the file the message names in the friends directory, then assess the standing again.

actions.label: Explain standing
actions.description: Explain a peer's standing in words, as input to a manual trust decision.
actions.agent: Explain a peer's earned standing in words: the tier with a human summary, why, and advisory notes that frame it as input to a MANUAL trust decision (not an instruction to change trust). Returns a StandingExplanation, or { ok:false, status:'not_found' } when the friend is missing.
actions.when: Putting a peer's track record to a person in words, as input to their own manual call on trust

errors.means: No friend record has that uuid or name, or two share the name, so there is no standing to explain.
errors.fix: Call list_friends with kind agent to find the peer, then explain its standing by id.

errors.means: The peer's record file, or its outcomes, could not be read when looked up by uuid; the message says why.
errors.fix: Check the file the message names in the friends directory, then explain the standing again.

actions.label: Get friend
actions.description: Look up one friend record.
actions.agent: Fetch a single friend record by uuid or by name.
actions.when: Reading one person's or agent's whole record, with its notes and linked identities, before acting on it

errors.means: No record has that uuid, and none was found by that name; a friends directory that can't be scanned also reads as not found.
errors.fix: Call list_friends to find the record, then call get_friend with its id.

errors.means: The record's file could not be read or parsed; the message says why.
errors.fix: Check the file the message names in the friends directory, then fetch the record again.

actions.label: List friends
actions.description: List the friend records, optionally filtered.
actions.agent: List friend records, optionally filtered by trust level and kind, optionally limited.
actions.when: Browsing everyone known, or narrowing to humans or agents at one trust level, before picking a record

errors.means: A record file could not be read; the message says why (a directory that can't be read lists as empty instead).
errors.fix: Check the file the message names in the friends directory, then list again.

limit.label: Limit
limit.description: max number of records to return

actions.label: Save note
actions.description: Save a friend's name, a tool preference or a note.
actions.agent: Save a friend's name, a tool preference, or a general note. Use override='true' to overwrite an existing value.
actions.when: Remembering something about someone: what to call them, which tool they prefer, or a keyed note

errors.means: The type is not name, tool_preference or note, the content is empty, or a tool_preference or note has no key.
errors.fix: Pass type name, tool_preference or note, a content value, and a key for tool_preference or note.

errors.means: No friend record has that uuid or name, or two share the name, so nothing was saved.
errors.fix: Call resolve_party or list_friends to find the record, then save the note with its uuid.

errors.means: A value is already saved under that key; the message shows it, and nothing changed.
errors.fix: Call again with override 'true' to replace it, or save it under another key.

errors.means: The store could not write the record; the message says why.
errors.fix: Check that the friends directory is writable, then save the note again.

override.label: Override
override.description: set to 'true' to overwrite an existing value

actions.label: Record interaction
actions.description: Record a turn with a friend: token usage and any shared-mission outcome.
actions.agent: Record a turn with a friend: accumulate token usage and/or append a shared-mission outcome (bumping familiarity).
actions.when: After a turn with someone: add the tokens it took to their total, or note how a mission you shared with them went

errors.means: Usage lacks a whole output_tokens of 0 or more, the outcome lacks a missionId or a result of success, partial or failed, or isn't for an agent; nothing saved.
errors.fix: Pass usage as { output_tokens: <whole number> }, and an outcome { missionId, result: success, partial or failed } only for an agent record.

errors.means: No friend record has that uuid or name, or two share the name, so nothing was saved.
errors.fix: Call resolve_party or list_friends to find the record, then record the turn with its uuid or name.

errors.means: The friend's record could not be read or written; the message says why, and usage may already be counted when the outcome write failed.
errors.fix: Call get_friend to see what was saved, check that the friends directory is writable, then record only what is missing.

usage.label: Usage
usage.description: token usage; only output_tokens is counted

actions.label: Upsert group
actions.description: Link a group's participants to it and remember them.
actions.agent: Upsert shared-group participant context: link each participant to the group, promoting strangers to acquaintances.
actions.when: Seeing several people in one group chat: tie each to the group, adding newcomers as acquaintances

errors.means: A participant has no externalId, or a record file could not be read or written; the message says why, and participants before it may already be saved.
errors.fix: Give every participant a provider and externalId, check the friends directory is writable, then upsert the same participants again.

actions.label: Set trust
actions.description: Set how much a friend is trusted.
actions.agent: Set a friend's trust level (also mirrors it onto the record's role).
actions.when: The owner decided how far someone is trusted: set their level, which their role then follows

errors.means: The trust level is missing or isn't family, friend, acquaintance or stranger, so nothing changed.
errors.fix: Pass trustLevel family, friend, acquaintance or stranger.

errors.means: No friend record has that uuid or name, so no trust changed.
errors.fix: Call list_friends to find the record, then set its trust by uuid or name.

errors.means: The record could not be written, or the audit line could not be appended after the new level was saved; the message says why.
errors.fix: Call get_friend to see which level the record holds, check that the friends directory and its _audit folder are writable, then set the trust again.

actions.label: Link identity
actions.description: Attach an external identity to a friend.
actions.agent: Link an external identity to a friend, merging any orphan record that already holds it (cross-channel unification): the orphan's notes and other ids move onto the friend and the orphan record is deleted. An id the friend already holds answers ok with status noop, or retry_unsupported when the store can't list records to finish an interrupted merge.
actions.when: One person reached you on another channel: attach that channel's id to their record, folding in any duplicate

errors.means: The externalId is empty or the provider isn't one friends knows, so nothing was linked.
errors.fix: Pass provider aad, local, teams-conversation, imessage-handle, email-address, a2a-agent or telegram-user, with a non-empty externalId.

errors.means: No friend record has that uuid or name, or two share the name, so nothing was linked.
errors.fix: Call list_friends to find the record, then link the identity to it by uuid.

errors.means: Another record holds the id, and merging it would move standing, authority or other ids between records, so it's the owner's call; nothing changed.
errors.fix: Show the owner both records with get_friend and let them decide; set_trust or unlink_identity can line the records up first.

errors.means: A record could not be read, written or deleted, or more than one record holds the id; the message says why, and a merge cut short leaves both.
errors.fix: If the message says the id is bound to several friends, unlink it from all but one; otherwise check the directory is writable and retry.

externalId.label: External id
externalId.description: the external identity within the provider

actions.label: Unlink identity
actions.description: Remove an external identity from a friend.
actions.agent: Remove an external identity from a friend.
actions.when: An external id was attached to the wrong person: detach that one provider id from their record

errors.means: No friend record has that uuid or name, or two share the name, so nothing was unlinked.
errors.fix: Call list_friends to find the record, then unlink the identity from it by uuid.

errors.means: The record has no identity with that provider and external id, so nothing changed.
errors.fix: Call get_friend to see the record's linked identities, then unlink one of those.

errors.means: The record could not be written; the message says why.
errors.fix: Check that the friends directory is writable, then unlink again.

provider.label: Provider
provider.description: identity provider, e.g. aad, local, teams-conversation, imessage-handle, email-address, a2a-agent

externalId.label: External id
externalId.description: the external identity within the provider

actions.label: Onboard agent
actions.description: Record another agent you can reach, from its coordinates.
actions.agent: Upsert an agent-peer friend record from already-resolved coordinates (no HTTP card fetch).
actions.when: Meeting another agent whose coordinates you already hold: keep its record, at stranger unless the owner names a level

errors.means: The name or agentId is empty, or the trust level isn't family, friend, acquaintance or stranger, so nothing was saved.
errors.fix: Pass the peer's name and a2a agentId, and leave trustLevel out or pass one of the four levels.

errors.means: The record could not be written, or the audit line for an explicit trust level could not be appended after the record was saved; the message says why.
errors.fix: Call list_friends with kind agent to see what was saved, check that the friends directory is writable, then onboard the agent again.

mailbox.label: Mailbox
mailbox.description: optional A2A git-mailbox coords { repo, selfOutboxAgentId }

actions.label: Connect to
actions.description: Link one of your own agents into this agent's fleet.
actions.agent: Management-sense control plane (brick 8): the owner links one of their OWN agents into this agent's fleet — introduce a peer by agentId/did/name at a trust level (default family for own-fleet). Authority-gated: commits inline ONLY from a local (owner-only stdio) or roster-verified same-account closed sense; from an open sense it downgrades to a confirm-prompt instead; a bare name with no resolvable handle/DID, no record hit, or more than one agent of that name returns needs_handle_or_introduction (it links only a target it can find). Writes one control-plane audit record (action:'connect') through the wired sink. Returns { ok:true, status:'connected', record } or { ok:false, status:'downgraded'|'needs_handle_or_introduction', downgrade? }.
actions.when: The owner, on this machine, links one of their own agents into this agent's fleet, by handle, DID or a name already known

errors.means: The trust level isn't family, friend, acquaintance or stranger, so nothing was linked.
errors.fix: Leave trustLevel out (family) or pass one of the four levels.

errors.means: The calling sense can't commit a link inline (an open or internal sense, or a closed one whose account membership wasn't verified); nothing was linked or audited.
errors.fix: Ask the owner to confirm the link from a local session, then connect again.

errors.means: No agentId was given and the DID or name matches no agent record, or the name matches more than one; nothing was linked.
errors.fix: Pass the peer's agentId, or onboard_agent it first, then connect again.

errors.means: The record could not be written, or the connect audit line could not be appended after the link was saved; the message says why.
errors.fix: Call list_friends with kind agent to see what was saved, check that the friends directory is writable, then connect again.

agentId.label: Agent id
agentId.description: the peer agent's join-key agentId (an owner-supplied handle)

did.label: DID
did.description: the peer's DID (an alternative handle; must resolve to an existing record)

name.label: Name
name.description: the peer's colloquial name (resolves ONLY by matching an existing record — never fabricated)

trustLevel.label: Trust level
trustLevel.description: the trust to link at (default family for own-fleet linked agents)

proof.label: Proof
proof.description: optional opaque proof slot (reserved; the TOFU path ignores it)

actions.label: Who am I
actions.description: Find out who the machine owner is.
actions.agent: Resolve who the machine owner is and which friend record represents the self.
actions.when: Finding out which OS user owns this machine and which friend record is that owner, else the first family record

errors.means: A record file could not be read while looking for the owner's record; the message says why.
errors.fix: Check the file the message names in the friends directory, then call whoami again.

actions.label: Channel capabilities
actions.description: Look up what a channel can carry.
actions.agent: Return the capabilities of a channel (integrations, markdown, streaming, rich cards, max length).
actions.when: Before writing for a channel: check whether it takes markdown, HTML, streaming or rich cards, and how long a message may be

errors.means: The channel is missing, or friends has no capabilities for that name, so none were returned; the message lists the channels it knows.
errors.fix: Call again with one of the channels the message lists, such as cli, teams, mail, a2a or mcp.

actions.label: Resolve room
actions.description: List who is in a group and how each is known.
actions.agent: Resolve a room (a group's external id) into its members, each with their trust context and how they're known (direct/group_only). Pure read.
actions.when: Before replying in a group chat: see who is in the room and how far each member is trusted

errors.means: A record file the room is built from could not be read; the message says why (a directory that can't be read gives an empty room instead).
errors.fix: Check the file the message names in the friends directory, then resolve the room again.

channel.label: Channel
channel.description: channel lens for the trust explanation (default mcp)

actions.label: Share profile
actions.description: Prepare a profile to send to another agent, within your consent.
actions.agent: Producer: prepare a consent-gated, scope-filtered, provenance-preserving profile-share envelope for another agent (names the party by join key, not the local uuid). Self identity comes from whoami. Returns { ok, envelope } or { ok:false, status }.
actions.when: Another agent should learn what this agent knows about someone, as far as the owner's consent policy allows

errors.means: The host built this server without a grant store, so it can't check consent and share; friends-mcp --dir always wires one.
errors.fix: Construct the server with a grant store (or run friends-mcp --dir <path>), then check consent and share again.

errors.means: The scope is not a share scope friends knows, so nothing was prepared.
errors.fix: Pass scope name, identity, notes:safe, notes:all or outcomes.

errors.means: No friend record has that uuid or name, or two share the name, or its file can't be read, so there is nothing to share.
errors.fix: Call list_friends to find the record, then share it by uuid.

errors.means: The consent policy refuses this scope to that recipient: name needs trust of friend or above, identity needs family or a grant, and the notes and outcomes scopes need a grant.
errors.fix: Ask the owner to grant_share the scope with the friend's uuid as subjectKey and this toAgentId; a grant can't unlock name, which needs a friend.

errors.means: A friend record or the grant store threw while the share was built; the message says why.
errors.fix: Check the file or folder the message names in the friends directory, then share the profile again.

actions.confirm: Prepare this scope of what you know about this person to send to that agent?

friendId.label: Friend
friendId.description: the local friend to share (uuid or name)

scope.label: Scope
scope.description: what to share: identity scopes carry only the join key; notes:* / outcomes require an explicit grant under the default tiered policy

proof.label: Proof
proof.description: optional opaque proof to stamp on the envelope (for a non-TOFU recipient verifier)

actions.label: Import profile
actions.description: Take in a profile another agent shared, without overwriting your own notes.
actions.agent: Consumer (non-clobbering merge): import a profile-share envelope. Resolves the party by join key; lands notes in importedNotes and an outcomes share's outcomes in importedOutcomes, both under the source agent, WITHOUT touching first-party notes or outcomes; source trust caps acceptance; the party's trust stays as it was. Returns { ok, status, record, importedOutcomes }.
actions.when: Another agent sent what it knows about someone: take its notes and outcomes in, kept apart from your own

errors.means: The envelope lacks a subject with a list of { provider, externalId } ids, its notes aren't a list of { key, value }, its outcomes aren't a list, or fromAgentId is empty.
errors.fix: Pass the envelope share_profile produced, as it arrived, with the sending agent's id as fromAgentId.

errors.means: trustOfSource is below acquaintance, or not a trust level, so the envelope was refused and nothing was imported.
errors.fix: Call describe_trust on the sending agent; import only from a source trusted at acquaintance or above.

errors.means: The envelope names someone with no record here, and only a friend or family source may introduce a new person; nothing was imported.
errors.fix: Find or create the person's record with resolve_party first, or ask a friend or family agent to introduce them.

errors.means: A friend record could not be read or written; the message says why.
errors.fix: Check the file the message names in the friends directory, then import again.

fromAgentId.label: From agent
fromAgentId.description: the agent the envelope arrived from (join-key agentId)

trustOfSource.label: Trust of source
trustOfSource.description: this agent's resolved trust in the source agent — the acceptance cap

actions.label: Grant share
actions.description: Let another agent receive a scope of your data, revocably.
actions.agent: Mint an explicit, revocable consent grant: an agent may receive a scope of a subject (a friend's profile, keyed by friend uuid; or a mission, keyed by its missionKey). The consent half of the moat.
actions.when: The owner agreed that one agent may receive one scope of a person's profile or of a mission

errors.means: The host built this server without a grant store, so it can't keep a grant; friends-mcp --dir always wires one.
errors.fix: Construct the server with a grant store (or run friends-mcp --dir <path>), then keep a grant again.

errors.means: The scope is not one friends knows, or expiresAt isn't a date, so no grant was made.
errors.fix: Pass scope identity, notes:safe, notes:all, outcomes or mission (the scopes a grant can unlock), and leave expiresAt out or pass an ISO date.

errors.means: The grant store could not write the grant; the message says why.
errors.fix: Check that the friends directory's _grants folder is writable, then grant again.

actions.confirm: Let that agent receive this scope from now on, until the grant expires or is revoked?

subjectKey.label: Subject
subjectKey.description: whose data may be shared — a local friend uuid for a profile, or a missionKey for a mission (the legacy arg name subjectFriendId is still accepted)

recipientAgentId.label: Recipient
recipientAgentId.description: the agent that may receive it (join-key agentId)

expiresAt.label: Expires
expiresAt.description: optional ISO expiry; absent ⇒ never expires

actions.label: Revoke share
actions.description: Withdraw a consent grant. The audit trail is kept.
actions.agent: Revoke a consent grant by id (tombstones it; the audit trail survives). The right-to-be-forgotten lever. Revoking a grant that is already revoked answers ok with status noop.
actions.when: The owner withdrew consent: stop one grant from letting an agent receive that scope any longer

errors.means: The host built this server without a grant store, so there is no grant to revoke; friends-mcp --dir always wires one.
errors.fix: Construct the server with a grant store (or run friends-mcp --dir <path>), then revoke again.

errors.means: The grant id isn't letters, digits, dots, underscores and hyphens starting with a letter or digit, so it can't name a grant; nothing changed.
errors.fix: Call list_shares and pass the id of the grant to revoke.

errors.means: No grant has that id, or its file can't be read or holds a scope friends doesn't know; nothing changed.
errors.fix: Call list_shares to find the grant's id, then revoke it.

errors.means: The grant store could not write the revocation; the message says why.
errors.fix: Check that the friends directory's _grants folder is writable, then revoke again.

actions.label: List shares
actions.description: List the consent grants and whether each still holds.
actions.agent: List consent grants with their effective state, optionally filtered by subject / recipient / effectiveness. The audit + revoke surface.
actions.when: Auditing who may receive what: every consent grant, or those for one subject or recipient, with its expiry state

errors.means: The host built this server without a grant store, so it can't list grants; friends-mcp --dir always wires one.
errors.fix: Construct the server with a grant store (or run friends-mcp --dir <path>), then list grants again.

subjectKey.label: Subject
subjectKey.description: filter to one subject — a friend uuid or a missionKey (the legacy arg name subjectFriendId is still accepted)

effectiveOnly.label: Effective only
effectiveOnly.description: set to 'true' to return only grants that currently consent

actions.label: Record mission
actions.description: Create or update a shared mission by its cross-agent key.
actions.agent: Upsert a shared mission (brick 3) by its cross-agent missionKey: create one when the key is unknown, else merge into the existing record. Appends first-party learnings / participants / outcomes and sets status. The mission analogue of record_interaction's outcome writer. Returns the saved mission record.
actions.when: Work with other agents moved on: keep the mission's status, who took part, and what you learned under its shared key

errors.means: The host built this server without a mission store, so there is no mission to record; friends-mcp --dir always wires one.
errors.fix: Construct the server with a mission store (or run friends-mcp --dir <path>), then record again.

errors.means: The missionKey is empty, the status isn't one of the five, or participants, learnings or outcomes isn't a list of the shape it takes; nothing was saved.
errors.fix: Pass a missionKey and a status of active, succeeded, partial, failed or abandoned, with each list shaped as its input describes.

errors.means: The mission file could not be written; the message says why.
errors.fix: Check that the friends directory's _missions folder is writable, then record again.

missionKey.label: Mission key
missionKey.description: the cross-agent join key for the mission (a ticket id / repo+PR / slugged name)

title.label: Title
title.description: human title; used only when CREATING (ignored on upsert)

participants.label: Participants
participants.description: agent attributions [{ agentId?, agentName? }], each naming at least one, merged deduped by agentId

learnings.label: Learnings
learnings.description: first-party learnings [{ key, value, shareable? }] appended to the mission

outcomes.label: Outcomes
outcomes.description: first-party outcomes [{ missionId, result, note? }] appended to the mission

actions.label: Get mission
actions.description: Look up one mission record.
actions.agent: Fetch a single mission record by its local uuid id.
actions.when: Reading one shared work record in full, with its learnings, outcomes and participants, by its local id

errors.means: The host built this server without a mission store, so it can't read a mission; friends-mcp --dir always wires one.
errors.fix: Construct the server with a mission store (or run friends-mcp --dir <path>), then read a mission again.

errors.means: No mission has that local id, or its file is unreadable or corrupt.
errors.fix: Call list_missions to find the mission's id, then fetch it.

actions.label: List missions
actions.description: List the mission records.
actions.agent: List mission records, optionally limited.
actions.when: Browsing every shared work record this agent keeps, to find one's local id or see what is open

errors.means: The host built this server without a mission store, so it can't list missions; friends-mcp --dir always wires one.
errors.fix: Construct the server with a mission store (or run friends-mcp --dir <path>), then list missions again.

limit.label: Limit
limit.description: max number of records to return

actions.label: Share mission
actions.description: Prepare a mission to send to another agent, within your consent.
actions.agent: Producer: prepare a consent-gated, scope-filtered, provenance-preserving mission-share envelope for another agent (names the mission by its missionKey, not the local uuid). Self identity comes from whoami. 'mission' carries the shareable learnings; 'outcomes' carries the mission's outcomes. Returns { ok, envelope } or { ok:false, status }.
actions.when: Passing what was learned on shared work, or how it turned out, to another agent that consent covers

errors.means: The host built this server without a mission store and grant store, so it can't share a mission; friends-mcp --dir always wires one.
errors.fix: Construct the server with a mission store and grant store (or run friends-mcp --dir <path>), then share a mission again.

errors.means: The scope is neither mission nor outcomes.
errors.fix: Pass scope mission for the shareable learnings, or outcomes for the outcomes.

errors.means: No mission has that local id, so there is nothing to share.
errors.fix: Call list_missions to find the mission's id, then share it.

errors.means: No effective grant covers this scope of the mission for that recipient; trust alone never unlocks mission or outcomes.
errors.fix: Ask the owner to grant_share the same scope with the mission's missionKey as subjectKey and this toAgentId, then share again.

errors.means: A store could not read the mission, records or grants the share is built from; the message says why.
errors.fix: Check that the friends directory is readable, then share the mission again.

actions.confirm: Prepare this scope of the mission to send to that agent?

missionId.label: Mission
missionId.description: the local mission to share (its local uuid id)

scope.label: Scope
scope.description: what to share: 'mission' (title/status + shareable learnings) or 'outcomes' (the result rows); both require an explicit grant under the tiered policy

proof.label: Proof
proof.description: optional opaque proof to stamp on the envelope (for a non-TOFU recipient verifier)

actions.label: Import mission
actions.description: Take in a mission another agent shared, without changing your own record.
actions.agent: Consumer (non-clobbering merge): import a mission-share envelope. Resolves the mission by missionKey; lands learnings in the imported namespace WITHOUT touching first-party learnings; append-merges + dedupes outcomes; source trust caps acceptance; leaves status/participants as they were. Returns { ok, status, record }.
actions.when: A peer agent sent a mission-share envelope: merge its learnings and outcomes in as that peer's claims

errors.means: The host built this server without a mission store, so it can't import a mission; friends-mcp --dir always wires one.
errors.fix: Construct the server with a mission store (or run friends-mcp --dir <path>), then import a mission again.

errors.means: No envelope object came with the call, so there is nothing to import.
errors.fix: Pass the MissionShareEnvelope the peer sent as envelope.

errors.means: trustOfSource is below acquaintance, or not a trust level, so the envelope was refused and nothing changed.
errors.fix: Call describe_trust on the sending agent; import only from a source trusted at acquaintance or above.

errors.means: The envelope names a mission this agent doesn't have, and only a friend or family source may start one here.
errors.fix: Record the mission first with record_mission, or accept new missions only from a friend or family agent.

errors.means: The envelope is malformed (no subject, or learnings that aren't a list), or the mission store could not write; the message says which.
errors.fix: Pass the envelope exactly as the peer sent it; if it is well formed, check that the friends directory's _missions folder is writable.

fromAgentId.label: From agent
fromAgentId.description: the agent the envelope arrived from (join-key agentId)

trustOfSource.label: Trust of source
trustOfSource.description: this agent's resolved trust in the source agent — the acceptance cap

actions.label: Coordinate
actions.description: Offer, accept, decline or hand off a mission to another agent.
actions.agent: Producer (brick 5): prepare a coordination message that negotiates WHO does a mission — one of request/offer/accept/decline/handoff, named by the mission's missionKey (not the local uuid). Consent-gated via the identity-tier 'coordinate' scope (trust ≥ friend suffices). 'accept' claims the assignment for self; 'handoff' (only by the agent holding the assignment) proposes a new assignee whose own accept confirms it (non-transitive). Self identity comes from whoami. Returns { ok, envelope } or { ok:false, status: not_found|no_consent|not_assignee }.
actions.when: Settling which agent takes a piece of shared work: ask, offer, accept, decline or hand it off

errors.means: The host built this server without a mission store and grant store, so it can't coordinate; friends-mcp --dir always wires one.
errors.fix: Construct the server with a mission store and grant store (or run friends-mcp --dir <path>), then coordinate again.

errors.means: The intent is not request, offer, accept, decline or handoff.
errors.fix: Pass intent request, offer, accept, decline or handoff.

errors.means: No mission has that local id, so there is nothing to coordinate.
errors.fix: Call list_missions to find the mission's id, then coordinate on it.

errors.means: The recipient is trusted below friend (an agent with no record counts as a stranger); a grant can't unlock the coordinate scope.
errors.fix: Coordinate with a friend or family agent, or ask the owner whether to raise that agent's trust to friend.

errors.means: A handoff came from an agent that doesn't hold the mission's assignment, so nothing was sent.
errors.fix: Call get_coordination to see who holds it; accept the mission first, or ask its holder to hand it off.

errors.means: A store could not read or write the mission, records or grants; the message says why.
errors.fix: Check that the friends directory is writable, then coordinate again.

actions.confirm: Prepare this coordination message about the mission for that agent?

missionId.label: Mission
missionId.description: the local mission to coordinate (its local uuid id)

intent.label: Intent
intent.description: the coordination verb: request (will you take this?) / offer (I'll take this) / accept (yes, I'm on it — sets assignee=self) / decline (no) / handoff (it's yours now — you must hold the assignment; proposes a new assignee)

note.label: Note
note.description: optional free text carried on the message + logged

proposedAssignee.label: Proposed assignee
proposedAssignee.description: the proposed new assignee { agentId?, agentName? } — meaningful ONLY on intent=handoff

task.label: Task
task.description: optional delegation task-spec { summary, details?, inputs? } — meaningful ONLY on intent=request (gap-2); the producer mints a requestId, stamps it on the envelope, and records the delegation first-party for the result-return to correlate against

proof.label: Proof
proof.description: optional opaque proof to stamp on the envelope (for a non-TOFU recipient verifier)

actions.label: Import coordination
actions.description: Take in a coordination message from another agent.
actions.agent: Consumer (brick 5, non-clobbering merge): import a coordination message. Resolves the mission by missionKey; appends the intent to coordination.log stamped origin:imported WITHOUT touching first-party learnings/notes/status; only an 'accept' sets the assignee (last-writer-wins by issuedAt); a 'handoff' doesn't set the assignee on its own (only an accept does); status/trust/standing stay as they were; source trust caps acceptance; a friend/family peer may seed an unknown mission. Returns { ok, status: logged|assigned|seeded, record } or { ok:false, status }.
actions.when: A peer agent sent a coordination message about shared work: log it, and take a newer accept as the assignee

errors.means: The host built this server without a mission store, so it can't import coordination; friends-mcp --dir always wires one.
errors.fix: Construct the server with a mission store (or run friends-mcp --dir <path>), then import coordination again.

errors.means: No envelope object came with the call, so there is nothing to import.
errors.fix: Pass the CoordinationEnvelope the peer sent as envelope.

errors.means: trustOfSource is below acquaintance, or not a trust level, so the message was refused and nothing changed.
errors.fix: Call describe_trust on the sending agent; import only from a source trusted at acquaintance or above.

errors.means: The message names a mission this agent doesn't have, and only a friend or family source may start one here.
errors.fix: Record the mission first with record_mission, or accept new missions only from a friend or family agent.

errors.means: The envelope is malformed (no subject), or the mission store could not write; the message says which.
errors.fix: Pass the envelope exactly as the peer sent it; if it is well formed, check that the friends directory's _missions folder is writable.

fromAgentId.label: From agent
fromAgentId.description: the agent the envelope arrived from (join-key agentId)

trustOfSource.label: Trust of source
trustOfSource.description: this agent's resolved trust in the source agent — the acceptance cap

actions.label: Get coordination
actions.description: See who holds a mission and its coordination log.
actions.agent: Read lens (brick 5): return a mission's coordination state — its current assignee (who holds it; absent ⇒ unclaimed) + the append-only log of every request/offer/accept/decline/handoff that flowed. Returns { assignee, assignedAt?, log } (the empty default { assignee: undefined, log: [] } when it has had no coordination), or { ok:false, status:'not_found' } when the mission is missing.
actions.when: Checking who currently holds a piece of shared work and every ask, offer and handoff so far

errors.means: The host built this server without a mission store, so it can't read coordination; friends-mcp --dir always wires one.
errors.fix: Construct the server with a mission store (or run friends-mcp --dir <path>), then read coordination again.

errors.means: No mission has that local id, or its file is unreadable or corrupt, so it has no coordination to show.
errors.fix: Call list_missions to find the mission's id, then read its coordination.

actions.label: Send result
actions.description: Return your finished work for a mission to the agent that delegated it.
actions.agent: Producer (gap-2 — the result-return): B returns its DELIVERABLE for a delegation, attributed to B (from whoami) + correlated to A's task-spec by requestId, named by the mission's missionKey (not the local uuid). Consent-gated via the identity-tier 'coordinate' scope (a result is B answering A's own delegation — trust ≥ friend suffices; NO new scope). Records the result first-party on B's own mission. Returns { ok, envelope } or { ok:false, status: not_found|no_consent }.
actions.when: Delegated work is finished: hand the deliverable back to the agent that asked, tied to its request id

errors.means: The host built this server without a mission store and grant store, so it can't return a result; friends-mcp --dir always wires one.
errors.fix: Construct the server with a mission store and grant store (or run friends-mcp --dir <path>), then return a result again.

errors.means: No mission has that local id, so there is nothing to answer.
errors.fix: Call list_missions to find the mission's id, then send the result on it.

errors.means: The requesting agent is trusted below friend; a grant can't unlock the coordinate scope a result travels under.
errors.fix: Send results only to a friend or family agent, or ask the owner whether to raise that agent's trust to friend.

errors.means: A store could not read or write the mission, records or grants; the message says why.
errors.fix: Check that the friends directory is writable, then send the result again.

actions.confirm: Record this result on the mission and prepare it for the agent that asked?

missionId.label: Mission
missionId.description: the local mission B is returning a result for (its local uuid id)

toAgentId.label: To agent
toAgentId.description: the recipient agent's join-key agentId — A, the delegator

requestId.label: Request
requestId.description: the delegation correlation key (the task-spec's requestId)

proof.label: Proof
proof.description: optional opaque proof to stamp on the envelope (for a non-TOFU recipient verifier)

actions.label: Import result
actions.description: Take in a result another agent returned for work you delegated.
actions.agent: Consumer (gap-2, non-clobbering merge): A imports B's result-return. Resolves the mission by missionKey; lands B's deliverable QUARANTINED + attributed under importedResults WITHOUT touching first-party; source trust caps acceptance (checked before correlation); a result whose requestId matches no prior first-party delegation is REJECTED (no_delegation — A only accepts results for work it delegated); an unknown mission is no_mission (only record_mission creates a mission); status and participants stay as A recorded them. Returns { ok, status, record } or { ok:false, status: untrusted_source|no_mission|no_delegation|assignee_mismatch|invalid }. A second result for a request already imported from that agent answers ok with status noop and keeps the first.
actions.when: An agent you gave work to sent back its result: take it in beside the mission, kept apart from your own

errors.means: The host built this server without a mission store, so there is no mission to land a result on; friends-mcp --dir always wires one.
errors.fix: Construct the server with a mission store (or run friends-mcp --dir <path>), then import again.

errors.means: The envelope is missing, or lacks subject.missionKey, a requestId, or a result with a summary whose requestId, if any, is the same; nothing landed.
errors.fix: Pass the envelope send_result produced, as it arrived.

errors.means: trustOfSource is below acquaintance, or not a trust level, so the result was refused and nothing landed.
errors.fix: Call describe_trust on the sending agent; import only from a source trusted at acquaintance or above.

errors.means: No mission here has the envelope's missionKey, and a result never creates one; nothing landed.
errors.fix: Call list_missions to check the key; record_mission the mission first only if this agent really delegated work on it.

errors.means: The mission has no delegation with the envelope's requestId, so this agent never asked for this result; nothing landed.
errors.fix: Call get_mission to see the mission's delegations; accept only results for work this agent delegated.

errors.means: The delegation went to a different agent than fromAgentId, or records no assignee, so the result is refused; nothing landed.
errors.fix: Call get_mission to see who the work was delegated to, and import only that agent's result.

errors.means: The mission file could not be read or written; the message says why.
errors.fix: Check that the friends directory's _missions folder is writable, then import again.

fromAgentId.label: From agent
fromAgentId.description: the agent the envelope arrived from (join-key agentId) — B

trustOfSource.label: Trust of source
trustOfSource.description: this agent's resolved trust in the source agent — the acceptance cap
